newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New Australian airline gains Asia, Europe rights.
newsitem.headline: New Australian airline gains Asia, Europe rights.

text.p: A new Australian airline gained approval on Wednesday to fly limited services to Sri Lanka, Greece and the Netherlands.
Australia's International Air Services Commission, which allocates flight rights negotiated from other countries, said it approved a plan by privately held Australia World Airways to fly the route.
"(The airline) is proposing two weekly services on the Australia - Sri Lanka - Greece - Netherlands route utilising a Boeing 767-300 aircraft," the commission said in a statement.
But approval was subject to the new airline securing A$25 million (US$19 million) in funding within six months, it said.
The commission was created after Canbera's 1992 decision to deregulate international air travel to Australia.
Before that decision, Qantas Airways Ltd was automatically entitled to all of the rights that Australia negotiated with other countries.
The commission initially rejected Australia World's proposal in January, saying it was dissatisfied with the airline's financial arrangements.
